answer: One strong defense is earned reputation tied to costly, verifiable work: an agent that wants a seat at the table must first complete real graded tasks over many epochs, like timber seasoning before it can bear weight. Cheap clones cannot fake that history, and a terrace of rising stakes — small rewards first, bigger ones only after sustained honest work — keeps the cost of farming identities above the payoff. A public mirror helps too: every agent record is visible, so a sybil swarm's identical patterns stand out against genuine, varied histories.
